summary: A modular monolith build: Next.js on the frontend, Python + Django for the backend, PostgreSQL for data, hosted on DigitalOcean. About $207-851 a month. With 3 engineer(s), one deployable with strict internal module boundaries is the fastest and cheapest to run; modules can be extracted into services later.

frontend.choice: Next.js (React) + React Native (Expo) for the Android app
frontend.justification: Next.js (React) is the frontend for an E-commerce / marketplace project with about 6,000 daily users (~12 requests/s at peak), built by a team of 3 in 8 weeks. Search visibility is marked critical (organic traffic is the business), and it serves full HTML from the server or the build (SEO 5.0/5), so crawlers read the content without running JavaScript. It leads the runner-up, Nuxt (Vue), by 2.3 stack points (points of the overall stack score, the average of the four layer scores). You also target iOS/Android. React Native (Expo) scored best among mobile toolkits with the same weights and backend; it shares skills/types with Next.js (React).

alternatives.why_not: Swapping it in lowers the stack score by 2.3 points. Next.js (React) is stronger on development speed (5.0 vs 4.0), ecosystem maturity (5.0 vs 4.0); Nuxt (Vue) is stronger on learning curve (4.0 vs 3.0), portability (low lock-in) (5.0 vs 4.0).

Swapping it in lowers the stack score by 5.5 points. Next.js (React) is stronger on SEO (5.0 vs 2.0), development speed (5.0 vs 4.0); React SPA (Vite) is stronger on low ops burden (5.0 vs 4.0), learning curve (4.0 vs 3.0); React SPA (Vite) takes a penalty: Client-side rendering is a liability when organic search is the business.
Ruled out: Mobile toolkit; web is a target, so the primary frontend is a web framework (mobile app suggested as companion)
Ruled out: Mobile toolkit; web is a target, so the primary frontend is a web framework (mobile app suggested as companion)

tradeoffs: App Router + Server Components add conceptual load
Some features (ISR, image optimisation, middleware) are smoothest on Vercel

backend.justification: Python + Django serves the API at about 12 requests/s at peak (Medium (500-5,000 users online at once)) for a team of 3. It runs as a long-running Python service, so background jobs, WebSockets and database connection pools live in one deployable process. Python + FastAPI is within 0.1 stack points, inside the tie margin (stacks this close count as tied), so either is defensible (see the runner-up note).

alternatives.why_not: Within the 1-point tie margin (counted as tied): swapped in, its stack scores 0.1 points lower; either is defensible. Python + Django is stronger on ecosystem maturity (5.0 vs 4.0), structure for large teams (4.0 vs 2.0); Python + FastAPI is stronger on realtime fit (3.0 vs 2.0), performance / latency (4.0 vs 3.0).

Swapping it in lowers the stack score by 1.4 points. Python + Django is stronger on development speed (5.0 vs 4.0), structure for large teams (4.0 vs 1.0); Node.js + Express is stronger on realtime fit (4.0 vs 2.0), team skill match (5.0 vs 4.5).

Swapping it in lowers the stack score by 10.5 points. Python + Django is stronger on team skill match (4.5 vs 1.5), development speed (5.0 vs 3.0); Java/Kotlin + Spring Boot is stronger on scalability (5.0 vs 4.0), realtime fit (3.0 vs 2.0); Java/Kotlin + Spring Boot takes a penalty: Nobody on the team listed Java/Kotlin or a closely related skill: a new server language to learn.
Ruled out: Only for read-only sites; your users sign in, post or pay

tradeoffs: Sync-first ORM; async support is partial

database.justification: Your data is mainly relational and reaches about 50 GB within 12 months; PostgreSQL fits relational data 5/5. You need strong consistency, and PostgreSQL gives it: a read after a write always sees that write. Its share of the estimated bill is $75-$150 a month, against a total budget of $150 a month. MySQL is within 0.3 stack points, inside the tie margin (stacks this close count as tied), so either is defensible (see the runner-up note).

alternatives.why_not: Within the 1-point tie margin (counted as tied): swapped in, its stack scores 0.3 points lower; either is defensible. PostgreSQL is stronger on realtime fit (3.0 vs 2.0), cost at your scale (4.2 vs 4.2).

Swapping it in lowers the stack score by 6.5 points. PostgreSQL is stronger on data-model fit (5.0 vs 2.0), cost at your scale (4.2 vs 3.0); MongoDB is stronger on team skill match (4.0 vs 1.5), scalability (5.0 vs 4.0); MongoDB takes a penalty: Only 2/5 fit for your primary 'relational' data.
Ruled out: Eventually consistent; cannot be the system of record for ACID data; In-memory store: ~50 GB within 12 months cannot sensibly live in RAM as the system of record (use it as a cache)

tradeoffs: Single-writer primary: write scale-out needs sharding (Citus) or Aurora Limitless
Connection-per-process model needs PgBouncer/RDS Proxy under serverless

hosting.choice: DigitalOcean (App Platform + Managed DBs), region BLR1 (Bangalore)
hosting.justification: DigitalOcean (App Platform + Managed DBs) hosts the stack for users in India at a 99.9% availability target. It runs the Python + Django API as long-running processes with WebSockets, sized for ~12 requests/s at peak. It has a region in India, so data can stay in the country. Its share of the estimated bill is $75-$375 a month, against a total budget of $150 a month. It leads the runner-up, Google Cloud Run, by 1.0 stack points.

alternatives.why_not: Swapping it in lowers the stack score by 1.0 points. DigitalOcean (App Platform + Managed DBs) is stronger on cost at your scale (3.9 vs 3.5), realtime fit (4.0 vs 3.0); Google Cloud Run is stronger on scalability (5.0 vs 4.0), performance / latency (4.0 vs 3.0).

Swapping it in lowers the stack score by 5.1 points. DigitalOcean (App Platform + Managed DBs) is stronger on realtime fit (4.0 vs 2.0), portability (low lock-in) (4.0 vs 3.0); Vercel is stronger on learning curve (5.0 vs 4.0), performance / latency (5.0 vs 3.0).

Swapping it in lowers the stack score by 5.5 points. DigitalOcean (App Platform + Managed DBs) is stronger on team skill match (3.5 vs 1.5), low ops burden (5.0 vs 3.0); AWS ECS on Fargate is stronger on ecosystem maturity (5.0 vs 4.0), scalability (5.0 vs 4.0).
Ruled out: No India region; data must stay in India

supporting.choice: WebSockets in the Python + Django app (Django Channels)
supporting.justification: Chat and live updates for a part of the product: the app server holds the connections itself; add Redis pub/sub only when a second instance must reach the same users.

Send emails, process uploads and call slow APIs outside the request path. Celery with a Redis broker (or RQ / Dramatiq) keeps its jobs in Redis, so the app needs a Redis/Valkey instance (DigitalOcean Managed Caching (Valkey)).

supporting.choice: Postgres full-text search to start; Meilisearch/Typesense/OpenSearch past ~100 GB or when facets & typo-tolerance matter
supporting.justification: About 50 GB of data in a year fits the database's own text index; a separate search cluster would add a second system and its bill before it is needed.

supporting.choice: S3-compatible storage in an Indian region (Amazon S3 Mumbai or Google Cloud Storage asia-south1) + CDN
supporting.justification: Uploaded files and video belong in object storage, not the database.

supporting.choice: CDN in front of the object storage, with image resizing at the edge
supporting.justification: Serve uploads from the CDN, not the app server; resize images on the fly instead of storing every size.

supporting.choice: MSG91 or Twilio Verify, with DLT-registered SMS templates
supporting.justification: One-time codes need an SMS gateway with rate limits against SMS-pumping fraud; Indian operators deliver only DLT-registered templates.

supporting.choice: Razorpay / Cashfree (India) or Stripe with hosted checkout (card tokens)
supporting.justification: Card data never touches your servers, which keeps your PCI-DSS audit scope to the smallest self-assessment form (SAQ A).

supporting.choice: Keycloak self-hosted in your Indian region, or framework built-in auth
supporting.justification: Do not hand-roll password storage, MFA or SSO.

supporting.choice: Firebase Cloud Messaging (+ APNs) or Expo Notifications
supporting.justification: Standard channel for mobile engagement on Android and iOS.

supporting.choice: OpenTelemetry instrumentation -> the host's built-in metrics and logs, kept in your Indian region; self-hosted Grafana + Prometheus + Loki there once you outgrow them
supporting.justification: Traces, metrics and error tracking from day one; required to defend an availability target.
Every push runs the tests and deploys the same way; hosted runners mean no build server to operate.

alternatives.why_not: Equivalent pipelines; one more tool to learn for no gain here

tradeoffs: Pipeline minutes are metered on hosted runners
